How do I read the time on a clock face?

Great question! A clock face has two main hands. The short hand is the hour hand and the long hand is the minute hand. When the long hand points to 12, we say o'clock; if the short hand is on 8, it is 8 o'clock. When the long hand points to 6, it is half past the hour. When it points to 3, it is quarter past, and on 9 it is quarter to the next hour. Each number on the clock stands for 5 minutes for the long hand. Practise reading the clock at home every morning!

What do a.m. and p.m. mean?

Good question! We use a.m. and p.m. to show whether a time is before or after midday. The letters a.m. mean the time from midnight to just before 12 noon, the morning hours. The letters p.m. mean the time from noon to just before midnight, the afternoon, evening and night. So you resume school at 8 a.m., eat lunch around 1 p.m., and go to bed maybe at 9 p.m. Without a.m. and p.m., saying 'the bus leaves at 7' would be confusing. Now you can tell time like an adult. Well done!

How many days are in a week, and how many weeks are in a year?

Nice question! There are 7 days in one week: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday. There are 52 weeks in one year. A year also has 12 months and 365 days, or 366 days in a leap year, which comes once every 4 years. Here is a quick check: 52 weeks × 7 days = 364 days, plus 1 extra day makes 365. Knowing the days and weeks helps you plan for school, market days and holidays. Learn the days in order and you will never be confused!

How do I remember the number of days in each month?

Great question! Use your knuckles! Make a fist and count the months on your knuckles and the dips between them. Every month on a knuckle has 31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October and December. Every month in a dip has 30 days, except February. April, June, September and November have 30 days. February is special with 28 days, or 29 in a leap year. You can also learn the rhyme 'Thirty days has September, April, June and November.' Try the knuckle trick now, it always works!

School starts at 8:00 a.m. and closes at 2:00 p.m. How long is the school day?

Let us count the hours together! From 8:00 a.m. to 12 noon is 4 hours. From 12 noon to 2:00 p.m. is 2 more hours. Add them: 4 + 2 = 6 hours. So the school day lasts 6 hours. When a time crosses from morning into afternoon, counting to 12 noon first makes it easy. You can use the same method for anything, like how long a journey from Kano to Kaduna takes. Counting time helps you plan your day well. Excellent work!

A football match starts at 4:00 p.m. and lasts 90 minutes. What time does it end?

Good thinking question! First change 90 minutes into hours and minutes. Since 60 minutes make 1 hour, 90 minutes is 1 hour and 30 minutes. Now add that to the starting time: 4:00 p.m. plus 1 hour is 5:00 p.m., then plus 30 minutes is 5:30 p.m. So the match ends at 5:30 p.m. This is how football fans in Nigeria know when to expect the final whistle. Breaking time into hours and minutes first makes adding easy. Keep practising, you are doing very well!

What is the difference between an analogue clock and a digital clock?

Nice observation question! An analogue clock has a round face with numbers 1 to 12 and moving hands, like the big clock on a church or mosque wall. You read it from where the hands point. A digital clock shows the time in numbers only, like 7:45, the way your phone or DSTV decoder shows it. Both tell the same time in different ways. Half past seven on an analogue clock is 7:30 on a digital clock. It is good to read both, so practise with any clock you find at home!

Amaka left home at 6:45 a.m. and reached school at 7:10 a.m. How long was her journey?

Let us find out together! From 6:45 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. is 15 minutes, because 60 − 45 = 15. From 7:00 a.m. to 7:10 a.m. is another 10 minutes. Add them: 15 + 10 = 25 minutes. So Amaka's journey took 25 minutes. Counting up to the next full hour first, then adding the rest, is the easiest way to find how long something takes. You can time your own walk to school tomorrow and work it out the same way. Well done!
